source: New for Sheepcliff (#41), migrated to the v2 card schema for #59 so the engine (#40) is built against it, not v1.
comment: The farm's event deck. The engine (packages/sim, #40) draws a card whose conditions hold, weighted live by its multipliers, respecting its limits; runs its start hooks; ends it after its duration with the end hooks. Every card has a beat the player sees within one second. Cozy only: nothing here hurts anyone. DL's birthday and first snow moved to events/authored.json for #59 (plan section 2 names them as the punctuation cards don't do); flockHuddle and farmerMeetsMerchant are new so the deck stays at fifteen.

timeScale.comment: One sim day is the clock's 180-second period when watching, so a sim minute is 0.125 real seconds and a sim hour is 7.5 real seconds. When away, a sim day is about a real day.

events.title: Fog morning
events.comment: The reference visibility event for #40. The flock huddles; DL counts them by ear. v2: conditions ported 1:1 from v1's preconditions; no multiplier, a fog roll is weather, not an actor state. #86 coverage: base weight raised 10 -> 22 — dawn had only this and farmersDayOff as reliable kinds (weather and dl-trick), and this is the one that gives a watch a weather-kind moment before the day's first draw of anything else.

start.comment: Fog layer over the field; the barn and the tree stay as shapes.

start.name: fog
start.comment: Sheep drift closer together; DL walks the edge of the field.

storybook.line: A fog came down at dawn and {dl} counted the flock by their bleats.

beat.start: The field greys out to shapes within a second; the flock bunches up.
beat.end: The fog thins from the top down and the barn's red comes back first.

events.title: Crows on the field
events.comment: Crows are data here and art in #47; DL's chase is sim work in #48. v2: flockSize.min becomes a ledger.flock condition; new causality, the issue's own example, crows are likelier when the hay is high — the Ledger has no separate hay stock, so this reads ledger.grass (the mean tuft level) as the stand-in, flagged to sim on #40. Base weight also drops from v1's flat 12 to 8: the new ×2 grass multiplier now carries the busy-hay-day likelihood the old flat number tried to bake in on its own, so the base has to sit lower to keep the same overall frequency once the multiplier can double it. #86 coverage: season widened to include spring (the bale reads on ledger.grass year-round, not only after a summer/autumn cut), and base raised 8 -> 18 alongside the deck's other daytime cards so a spring watch has real competition for merchantCaravan at midday instead of a near-default draw.

multipliers.comment: Plenty of grazing left standing reads as hay worth stealing.

start.comment: Three crows land on and around the hay bale.
The sheep do not like being watched.

end.comment: She chased them off. Good dog.

storybook.line: Three crows landed on the hay and {dl} sent them packing.

beat.start: Three crows drop onto the hay bale; the nearest sheep backs off a step.
beat.end: DL runs at them, they scatter over the fence, she trots back with her tail up.

events.title: Lost lamb
events.comment: Reference event for #40: a lamb wanders off the field at dusk and DL fetches it home. v2: this is the issue's own worked example. The hard gate stays dusk-only, sun or rain, so the storybook line stays true (it always happens near dusk); the three named actor predicates now do the causal work v1 could only fake with a flat weight of 8. `lambFarFromMother` is PROPOSED to sim on #40: today's sim springs every lamb to a fixed point behind its mother every tick with no detachment behaviour, so this predicate cannot yet be true and the card cannot yet fire on it — the multiplier is written for the sim #40 will build, not the one that exists today.

multipliers.comment: This is what "lost" means; the strongest driver, once sim on #40 can produce it (see the card comment: PROPOSED, not true in today's sim).
DL was not close enough to notice it slip out.

start.name: lambLost
start.comment: The sim picks a lamb and walks it out past the outer gate; DL's fetch-the-lamb behaviour reads this.
Its mother calls.

storybook.line: {lamb} wandered off at dusk and {dl} brought them home before dark.

beat.start: A lamb slips out the gate; its mother stands up and bleats after it.
beat.end: DL walks the lamb back through the gate, slowly, right behind it, and the ewe meets them.

events.title: Merchant caravan
events.comment: Owner's decision 12 (2026-09-08, plan section 11): the economy is not the farm's, no transaction happens on the farm. The caravan is now a road event, a passer-by, not a sale: any season, daytime, a decent gap, replacing the old `merchantPresent`+`[day,dusk]` trade-visit reading. Cooldown and duration are unchanged from the prototype's merchant cadence (balance merchant.everyMs / stayMs) so the gap stays a decent one, even though it is no longer measuring a trade cycle. Data stays honest: no coins hook here, same as before; base weight also drops 14 -> 10 now that other daytime cards carry more of the deck's weight (#86 coverage), so this card no longer wins the great majority of daytime draws by default. KNOWN GAP for the sim half of #86: this id is one of the four reference cards with code behind it (`packages/sim/src/engine/hooks.ts` REFERENCE_EFFECTS.merchantCaravan.start still calls `summonMerchant` unconditionally, whose job plan in `packages/sim/src/npcs.ts` still runs a `trade` job that silently sells the whole wool bank for coins and buys upgrades on every draw of this card). That code path is packages/sim, out of this lane's reach; retiring it, and moving the sale to the farmer's dawn market walk per the issue, is the sim half of #86. Until it lands, drawing this card still empties the wool bank in the running sim even though nothing below asks for that.

conditions.comment: Daytime only now (was day or dusk): a road event has no reason to keep the old trade window, and 'daytime' is the issue's own word for it.

start.comment: Puts the cart on the lane so the moment has a beat to see. No coins hook, no wool hook: the farm's stock does not move from this card's own data. See the card comment for the known code-path gap this alone cannot close.

storybook.line: A caravan rolled along the lane and {dl} trotted the fence to watch it pass.

beat.start: The cart rolls along the lane past the outer gate; the sheep look up and DL trots to the fence.
beat.end: The cart carries on down the lane and out of sight; the flock goes back to grazing.

events.title: Shearing day
events.comment: Reference event for #40: the sim tops every fleece up to ready and summons the farmer, who shears the lot. v2: flockSize.min becomes ledger.flock; new ledger.wool condition and multiplier so shearing day is triggered by a flock that is genuinely close to ready, not only by season and a coin flip.

conditions.comment: The flock's mean fleece is already more than half grown; this is a day whose time has come, not a random draw.

multipliers.comment: The fuller the flock already is, the readier the day.

start.name: shearingDay
start.comment: Every fleece is ready; the farmer's shear job keeps re-queuing until the field is trim.
An extra visit outside farmer.visitsAt.

storybook.line: Shearing day. The farmer clipped {flock} fleeces and the sheep felt the breeze.

beat.start: Every sheep on the field goes fluffy at once; the farmer walks in with the shears bubble.
beat.end: The last sheep is trim, the wool bank is full, and the flock does a little hop.

events.title: Rainbow after rain
events.comment: v1 proposed a bespoke `recentWeather` precondition beyond the issue's list; v2 carries the same idea forward as an ordinary predicate, `simMinutesSinceRain`, so it fits the ordinary {on, op, value} shape instead of a one-off object. Still PROPOSED to sim on #40, same as v1 flagged it. #86 coverage: base raised 12 -> 24 so a rain patch reliably resolves into this weather-kind moment rather than being outweighed by the day/dusk cards that do not need rain to fire.

start.name: rainbow
start.comment: A rainbow arc over the barn on the weather layer.

storybook.line: The rain stopped and a rainbow stood over the barn for a while.

beat.start: The arc fades in over the barn as the last drops fall; the sheep come out of the doorway.
beat.end: It fades from the outside in and is gone.

events.title: A stray cat visits
events.comment: The cat is a new creature: data here, art and behaviour in their own tickets (High gate). v2: new flockScattered multiplier, a calm settled flock reads as safer for a cat to approach. #86 coverage: weather widened from sun-only to sun or rain (still no snow — a cat has better sense). Every other dusk/night card either needs a lamb, needs rain specifically (flockHuddle), or is rare by design (farmerMeetsMerchant), so a rain stretch at dusk or night otherwise leaves nothing eligible at all. Base weight is unchanged: this card was already one of the two that dominated every measured population, and raising it further crowded out the very variety #86 is asking for (measured: it costs three-kind seeds rather than buying them), so wider weather is this card's whole contribution here.

multipliers.comment: A settled flock is a quieter field for a cautious visitor.

start.comment: Walks in along the fence and settles on the post nearest the gate.

storybook.line: A stray cat sat on the fence at dusk. {dl} pretended not to care.

beat.start: A cat pads in along the fence; DL freezes mid-step and stares.
beat.end: The cat hops down and leaves the way it came; DL does a stretch as if she meant it.

events.title: The farmer's day off
events.comment: Fires at dawn so both of the farmer's visits (farmer.visitsAt) are skipped. DL walks the farmer's rounds instead. v2: adds a farmerPresent condition — he cannot take the day off if he is already on the field. #86 coverage: base raised 6 -> 14 — dawn's other reliable card (fogMorning) needs sun and excludes summer, so this is the one dawn moment that holds up whatever the weather and the season.

start.name: farmerAway
start.comment: The farmer's clock schedule is skipped while set; DL visits the trough, the hay, and each sheep in turn.
Nobody topped up the trough.

storybook.line: The farmer took the day off, so {dl} did the rounds herself.

beat.start: The gate stays shut at the usual time; DL trots to the trough and looks into it.
beat.end: The farmer is back next morning with a heart bubble for DL.

events.title: Night of the fireflies
events.comment: Fireflies exist as small life from #33; this card brings a swarm. DL snaps at them and catches none. v2: new flockScattered multiplier, the swarm is easier to notice, and DL freer to chase it, on a settled night. #86 coverage: season widened from summer-only to spring, summer and autumn (warm-enough nights either side of summer — winter stays excluded, no fireflies in the snow), and base raised 10 -> 26 alongside stargazingNight so a clear night has two competing dl-trick/weather options instead of one — measured (packages/content/src/deck-coverage.test.ts) as the single biggest lever on the three-distinct-kinds population, since a night in spring previously had only strayCatVisits to draw.

multipliers.comment: A settled flock means DL is free to bounce after lights instead of minding sheep.

start.comment: A drifting swarm from the tree across the field.

start.name: fireflies
start.comment: DL's idle play prefers snapping at fireflies while set.

storybook.line: Fireflies filled the field and {dl} snapped at every one and caught none.

beat.start: A dozen lights blink on around the tree and drift out; DL bounces after the nearest.
beat.end: The lights thin out one by one and DL sits down, panting.

events.title: Lamb zoomies hour
events.comment: Short and daft. Every lamb runs rings round the trough; the ewes do not move. v2: new flockScattered multiplier, a lamb only feels safe enough to bolt for fun when the flock is not on edge. #86 coverage: timeOfDay widened to include dawn (a lamb fresh off a night's sleep is at least as likely to bolt as one in the afternoon sun). Base raised 12 -> 16, a smaller lift than most of this pass's: measured (deck-coverage.test.ts), pushing it much higher crowded out other day/dusk cards' kinds on the same seeds it was meant to help — a lamb that already draws often does not need to draw even more often to be seen.

multipliers.comment: A calm flock, not a stressed one, is when a lamb plays.

start.name: zoomies
start.comment: Lambs run laps of the trough at DL's run speed; DL may join.

storybook.line: {lamb} got the zoomies and ran rings round the trough.

beat.start: A lamb bolts from its mother's side and tears round the trough.
beat.end: It stops dead, wobbles, and lies down next to its mother.

events.title: The well runs low
events.comment: A hot dry spell. The trough is drawn low and the sheep queue at it until the farmer comes with buckets. Drop bubble is an art ask. v2: flockSize.min becomes ledger.flock; new ledger.grass condition so this is a genuine dry spell, not any sunny summer day, plus a farmerPresent multiplier — it worsens fastest with nobody around to catch it early.

conditions.comment: The mean tuft level reads parched, not just dry-ish.

multipliers.comment: Nobody around yet to top it up before it gets bad.

start.name: troughLow
start.comment: The trough draws empty; drinking gives less; sheep gather round it.

end.comment: An extra visit: the farmer walks in and the trough job refills it.

storybook.line: The well ran low in the heat until the farmer came with buckets.

beat.start: The trough's water drops to a line; a drop bubble over the nearest sheep.
beat.end: The farmer walks in, tops it up, and the queue breaks up drinking.

events.title: A windfall
events.comment: Owner's decision 12 (2026-09-08, plan section 11): no transaction happens on the farm, and this is the card the decision names by name ("the windfall, the dug-up purse"). No settlement stock exists yet to route the coins to (checked: neither the schema's conditionOn/hook vocabulary nor the sim's state carry one, only ledger.coins, the farm's own bank), so per the decision's own fallback this becomes a moment with no stock change rather than a purse of coins: DL still digs something up, it is just never coins any more. The old ledger.coins<=40 condition ("a find lands better on a lean bank") went with the coins hook it justified; nothing here reads the farm's coin bank any more. Kept the title and id (both otherwise pinned in packages/sim/test/engine-events.test.ts's eviction-line text, a sim-owned pin this lane does not move) even though the find itself no longer pays out. #86 coverage: timeOfDay widened to include dawn, and base raised 5 -> 14, so dawn keeps a bubble-kind option alongside fogMorning's weather and farmersDayOff's dl-trick.

start.comment: The find itself is the moment; no coins hook, no ledger stock moves.

storybook.line: {dl} dug up something bright by the tree, and nobody asked whose it was.

beat.start: DL digs at the foot of the tree and comes up with something in her teeth.
beat.end: She trots back to the field with her nose muddy, pleased with herself.

events.title: Stargazing night
events.comment: A clear night. Everybody lies down and looks up; the sky layer brightens its stars. v2: new flockScattered multiplier, a settled flock is what lies down together. #86 coverage: season widened from summer/autumn to all four — a clear night happens in any season, and this was the only card that could give spring and winter nights a second kind alongside strayCatVisits. Base raised 8 -> 26 alongside nightOfTheFireflies, together the single biggest lever measured (deck-coverage.test.ts) on the three-distinct-kinds population. Moment kind moved from dl-trick to weather: nobody does anything here (DL only sits and watches, same as the sky itself brightening), which is the fogMorning/rainbowAfterRain shape, not the crow-chase/cat-standoff one, and it is what turns a spring or winter night into a weather-kind moment instead of another dl-trick.

multipliers.comment: A scattered flock does not settle down together to watch the sky.

start.name: starsBright
start.comment: More and brighter stars on the night sky; sheep lie down facing up; DL sits by the gate.

storybook.line: A clear night. {dl} sat by the gate and watched the stars with the flock.

beat.start: The stars come up bright; DL sits down by the gate with her head tipped back.
beat.end: The sky dims to its usual night and DL walks to the barn door to sleep.

events.title: Rain, and a flock to gather
events.comment: New for #59, filling the seat DL's birthday and first snow left behind. Dramatises DL's own rain-shepherd priority (plan section 2, her fixed priority order: fetch, manual, riding, rain shepherd, dusk and dawn routine, idle play) as a watchable card instead of an unremarked background rule: the flock startling apart at the first drops, and DL running the flockScattered predicate down to zero. #86 coverage: base raised 9 -> 18 — this is the deck's only card that wants rain rather than merely allowing it, and it has no time-of-day gate at all, so it is the one dependable moment across every rainy stretch, whatever the season or the hour.

multipliers.comment: A bigger job, a bigger moment, when she has further to run.

start.name: gathering
start.comment: DL's rain-shepherd priority reads this and beelines for the furthest sheep first.
Rain, and no one gathering them in yet.

end.comment: Safe and dry under the barn eave.

storybook.line: Rain caught the flock scattered and {dl} gathered every one of them in.

beat.start: The rain starts and the flock startles apart; DL breaks into a run toward the furthest one.
beat.end: The last sheep is walked in under the barn eave and DL circles the group once, checking.

events.title: The farmer meets the merchant
events.comment: New for #59, filling the seat DL's birthday and first snow left behind. Shows off an AND of two actor predicates rather than a single one: merchantPresent and farmerPresent both true is already rare on its own, so the base weight is low and needs no multiplier.

start.name: crossing
start.comment: Cosmetic only: the two NPCs pause to talk instead of following their separate plans for a moment.

end.comment: Two of her favourite visitors at once.

storybook.line: The farmer and the merchant crossed paths on the lane and {dl} sat between them.

beat.start: The merchant's cart rolls in just as the farmer is finishing his rounds; they stop to talk.
beat.end: They go their separate ways, the farmer to the gate, the cart down the lane, and DL trots off after her nose.
